subject.title: feat(skill-workshop): add restore action for quarantined proposals and display scan findings

question: Should an operator-admin restore move a quarantined proposal back to pending when its fresh scan is still non-clean, relying on visible findings and the existing apply-time scanner gate?
rationale: The implementation does not execute unsafe content, but it changes the meaning and client-visible lifecycle of a security quarantine state; repository evidence does not establish that policy choice without owner intent.

options.title: Approve rescanned pending state
options.body: Allow explicit operator restore to reopen the proposal for revision while keeping findings visible and retaining service-side revalidation at apply time.

options.title: Require clean restore
options.body: Keep the proposal quarantined unless the fresh scan is clean, which preserves a stronger status invariant but does not provide a useful repair path for unchanged unsafe content.

options.title: Revise while quarantined
options.body: Add a quarantined-only revision path and transition to pending after revision, avoiding a pending record whose scan is still non-clean at the cost of a broader lifecycle change.

recommendation.title: Approve rescanned pending state
recommendation.body: Allow explicit operator restore to reopen the proposal for revision while keeping findings visible and retaining service-side revalidation at apply time.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Skill Workshop security-boundary work makes this the strongest available owner signal for accepting the quarantine transition.
